Unit 19 – Grammar

Questions / question tags / indirect questions · 10 exercises · Click a tab to start

Exercise A – Choose the correct answer
Choose the best option A, B, C or D to complete each question.
  • 1. Oh, I'm sorry! ………… disturbing you?
    ✓ D Am I (present continuous question: Am I disturbing you?)
  • 2. Did Dorothy ………… you about the meeting on Friday?
    ✓ A told (Did + past participle form: told)
  • 3. ………… hot when you were in Spain?
    ✓ B It was (exclamatory: It was hot! — not an inversion question here)
  • 4. Tony, ………… got time to call Mrs Roberts?
    ✓ D have you (have you got = do you have)
  • 5. When your boss arrived, ………… finished the report?
    ✓ C had you (When your boss arrived, had you finished = past perfect question)
  • 6. I know Jane's pretty, but ………… seen someone spend so much time in front of the mirror?
    ✓ C have you ever (present perfect question: have you ever seen)
  • 7. It's raining, so ………… cancel the concert?
    ✓ D are they (It's raining, so are they going to cancel the concert?)
  • 8. ………… pass me the salt, please?
    ✓ D Could you (polite request: Could you pass me...)
  • 9. Sir, ………… repeat what the homework is, please?
    ✓ D can you (Can you repeat... = polite request)
  • 10. ………… the couple you met in France last year staying at the same hotel?
    ✓ C Were (Were the couple... staying = past continuous question)
  • 11. I know how to pronounce 'controversy', but what ………… ?
    ✓ B it means (indirect question after "what": what it means)
  • 12. It's a great idea, but ………… it will work?
    ✓ B do you think (do you think it will work? — direct question)
Exercise B – Write questions
Use the prompts to write a correct question.
  • 1. you / wash / your hair / when I rang?
    ✓ Were you washing your hair when I rang?
  • 2. Julie / give / you / her e-mail address / yesterday?
    ✓ Did Julie give you her e-mail address yesterday?
  • 3. you / always / have / lunch / this late?
    ✓ Do you always have lunch this late?
  • 4. Jack and Tom / come / to the party / tonight?
    ✓ Are Jack and Tom coming to the party tonight?
  • 5. you / can / give / me / a hand / later?
    ✓ Can you give me a hand later?
  • 6. how / you / spell / your name?
    ✓ How do you spell your name?
  • 7. why / the government / can't / do / something / about the situation?
    ✓ Why can't the government do something about the situation?
  • 8. where / you / go / for your honeymoon / last year?
    ✓ Where did you go for your honeymoon last year?
  • 9. what / your house / look like / when / it is finished?
    ✓ What will your house look like when it is finished?
  • 10. which / flavour of ice cream / your favourite / be?
    ✓ Which flavour of ice cream is your favourite?
Exercise C – Complete using the words in the box (one extra)
Use each word only once. There is one extra word you do not need to use.
Word bank (use each once – one is extra):
who where which whose what whom how when why
HELP US HELP THE ENVIRONMENT

(1) responsibility is it to look after the environment? Yours! And (2) should you start? Right now is the answer! But (3) is going to help you? We are! We are GreenWarriors, the environmental protest group, and we know the answers to all your questions. We've put together this factsheet to get you started.

(4) me? We all have a responsibility to the world around us. Ordinary people like you can make a big difference.

But (5) can I make a difference? By recycling your paper, glass and plastic and by taking part in GreenWarrior demonstrations and protests in your area.

(6) 's the first step? The first step is to come along to the GreenWarrior offices and speak to one of our officers. They will let you know about the next protest in your area.

(7) other organisations are you connected to? GreenWarriors is a completely independent protest organisation.

(8) is GreenWarriors based? We are a national organisation, with our headquarters in Northampton.

✓ (1) whose  (2) when  (3) who  (4) why  (5) how  (6) what  (7) which  (8) where  [extra: whom]
Exercise D – Circle the correct phrase
Choose the correct form — subject question or object question.
  • 1. 'Who to the party?' 'Maria, but she told me she couldn't come.'
    ✓ asked you (Who = subject; who asked you = subject question, no auxiliary needed)
  • 2. 'Who at the supermarket?' 'Just Ben, but I don't think he saw me.'
    ✓ did you see (you saw someone = object question; who did you see?)
  • 3. 'What the impression that Greg was depressed?' 'Oh, I don't know. He just seemed a bit down.'
    ✓ gave you (What gave you = subject question; what = subject)
  • 4. 'Who had stolen the money?' 'Jenny, but she believed me when I told her I hadn't done it.'
    ✓ thought you (Who thought you had stolen = subject question)
  • 5. 'Which programme the most?' 'Well, I learned a lot from Extreme History.'
    ✓ taught you (Which programme = subject; the programme taught you)
  • 6. 'Who this book from?' 'Tracy, and I need to give it back to her tomorrow.'
    ✓ did you borrow (you borrowed the book = object question)
  • 7. 'What to this part of the world?' 'Work, really, and I've always loved this country.'
    ✓ brought you (What brought you = subject question; what = subject)
  • 8. 'Who of starting the fight?' 'He says that John started it by calling him names.'
    ✓ accused George (Who accused George = subject question)
  • 9. 'Which person the most?' 'I think I would say my grandmother because she's worked hard all her life.'
    ✓ do you admire (you admire someone = object question)
  • 10. 'Who your secret?' 'I'm not sure, but I think Simone probably told him.'
    ✓ told Dave (Who told Dave = subject question)
Exercise E – Write one word in each gap
Complete the passage "Early humans and the weather" with one word in each numbered gap.
Early humans and the weather

(1) you think you understand the weather? For early humans, the weather was a constant source of questions. (2) is it raining? What (3) this storm mean? Where (4) the wind go when it blows? People came up with many explanations for the weather, usually involving gods or ancestors. (5) you explain what a rainbow is? The Cherokee people of America believed that it was the hem of the sun god's coat.

The weather has also been used to explain other things. What would you say if someone asked you (6) kangaroos come from? You'd probably say Australia, but (7) did the Aborigines explain these strange animals? They told a story about a great storm. A group of Aboriginal hunters watched in amazement as the wind blew large creatures over their heads. (8) could they be? Finally, the wind died down and the kangaroos landed on the ground. The storm had brought them a new animal to hunt.

✓ (1) Do  (2) Why  (3) does  (4) does  (5) Can  (6) where  (7) how  (8) What

Exercise G – Complete the question tags
Write the missing word to complete each question tag.
  • 1. Get me some chewing gum when you go to the shop, you?
    ✓ will (imperative → will you?)
  • 2. Let's watch that new DVD you bought today, we?
    ✓ shall (Let's... → shall we?)
  • 3. There's not really much point waiting, there?
    ✓ is (There's = There is → is there?)
  • 4. Tonia will put us up for the weekend, she?
    ✓ won't (positive statement → negative tag: won't she?)
  • 5. Nobody seems to like Jessica, they?
    ✓ do (Nobody = negative → positive tag: do they?)
  • 6. I'm not making much sense now, I?
    ✓ am (I'm not → positive tag: am I?)
  • 7. Let's go because it's getting late, it?
    ✓ isn't (it's getting late → isn't it?)
  • 8. If you borrow my coat, don't get it dirty, you?
    ✓ will (negative imperative → will you?)
  • 9. Bill should be here by now, he?
    ✓ shouldn't (should → shouldn't he?)
  • 10. I'm making you feel uncomfortable, I?
    ✓ am (I'm + positive → negative tag: am I not? shortened to am I in informal)
  • 11. Someone left the door open, they?
    ✓ didn't (someone → they; past simple positive → negative tag: didn't they?)
  • 12. Nobody knows about this, they?
    ✓ do (Nobody = negative → positive tag: do they?)
Exercise H – Rewrite the sentences correctly
Each sentence contains an error in an indirect question. Rewrite it correctly.
  • 1. I wonder if you could tell me what time does the plane from Frankfurt arrive?
    ✓ I wonder if you could tell me what time the plane from Frankfurt arrives.
  • 2. Could you let me know when would you like me to come for an interview.
    ✓ Could you let me know when you would like me to come for an interview?
  • 3. I wonder if you know what bus should I catch for the town centre.
    ✓ I wonder if you know what bus I should catch for the town centre.
  • 4. Do you think you could tell me how do you work this ticket machine?
    ✓ Do you think you could tell me how you work this ticket machine?
  • 5. I wonder you have seen George?
    ✓ I wonder if you have seen George.
  • 6. I would like to know do you have any double rooms?
    ✓ I would like to know if / whether you have any double rooms.
  • 7. Can you tell me what were you doing in my office?
    ✓ Can you tell me what you were doing in my office?
  • 8. Do you know where is this address?
    ✓ Do you know where this address is?
Exercise I – Sentence transformation
Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words in each gap.
  • 1.
    When does Tina get back from Berlin? KNOW
    Do from Berlin?
    ✓ you know when Tina gets (back from Berlin)
  • 2.
    What time does the film start tonight? STARTS
    Could you tell me tonight?
    ✓ what time the film starts tonight
  • 3.
    Is service included in the price? KNOW
    I would like to in the price.
    ✓ know if / whether service is included
  • 4.
    What is the salary? LET
    Could you the salary is?
    ✓ let me know what (the salary is)
  • 5.
    Have you been to Brussels before? WONDER
    I to Brussels before.
    ✓ wonder if you have been
  • 6.
    Did Gail pass her exam? PASSED
    Do you her exam?
    ✓ know if Gail passed / know whether Gail passed
  • 7.
    I wonder if you know where Mary went after the party last night. GO
    Where after the party last night?
    ✓ did Mary go (after the party last night)
  • 8.
    I would like to know how many days holiday we get each year. GIVEN
    How many days holiday each year?
    ✓ are we given (each year)
Exercise J – Circle the extra word in each sentence
Each sentence has one word which should not be there. Write the extra word in the box.
  • 1. Do you have much free time these days or are you be quite busy?
    ✓ be (extra: "are you be" → should be "are you")
  • 2. I would like to know it when I can expect my order to be delivered.
    ✓ it (extra: "know it when" → should be "know when")
  • 3. Do you think whether you could possibly let me know how soon you will have the work finished?
    ✓ whether (extra: "think whether you" → should be "think you")
  • 4. I wonder if you know who it is responsible for cleaning the building.
    ✓ it (extra: "who it is responsible" → should be "who is responsible")
  • 5. Tell Roger who did you saw when you were at the police station the other day.
    ✓ did (extra: "who did you saw" → should be "who you saw")
  • 6. Did Dad mention who he sold him the car to?
    ✓ him (extra: "sold him the car" → should be "sold the car")
  • 7. You shouldn't leave your homework to the very last minute if you want to get a good mark, should not you?
    ✓ not (extra: "should not you?" → should be "should you?" — negative tag after negative statement)
  • 8. I wonder it if you know where I can buy something to eat.
    ✓ it (extra: "wonder it if" → should be "wonder if")
